title.value: Turn product photos into video ads with an ad agent

introduction.value: A commenter feeds product photos and audience details to an agent that drafts the script, generates b-roll, and adds voiceover; another mentions a bot organizing calendar and payments.

method.value: One commenter said they give a dedicated ad agent raw product photos plus an audience demographic, and it handles a first pass end to end: drafting the script, generating b-roll, and adding voiceover. They do not leave it fully unattended; the useful part is that the agent outputs the exact prompt for each scene, so the person can fix only the bad scene and re-run that clip instead of reworking the whole ad.

outcome.value: They said this makes the workflow usable and saves them from spending 20 minutes wrestling with a general LLM on every fix. The limitation they stressed is that unguided output is still generic, so it is not a hands-off system.

notes.value: A separate commenter said a friend's driving-school bot only handled repetitive admin, funneling messages and appointments while organizing calendar and payment data into a database.

source_text.body:
Turn product photos into video ads with an ad agent
A commenter feeds product photos and audience details to an agent that drafts the script, generates b-roll, and adds voiceover; another mentions a bot organizing calendar and payments.
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
One commenter said they give a dedicated ad agent raw product photos plus an audience demographic, and it handles a first pass end to end: drafting the script, generating b-roll, and adding voiceover. They do not leave it fully unattended; the useful part is that the agent outputs the exact prompt for each scene, so the person can fix only the bad scene and re-run that clip instead of reworking the whole ad.
How it went
They said this makes the workflow usable and saves them from spending 20 minutes wrestling with a general LLM on every fix. The limitation they stressed is that unguided output is still generic, so it is not a hands-off system.
Worth knowing
A separate commenter said a friend's driving-school bot only handled repetitive admin, funneling messages and appointments while organizing calendar and payment data into a database.
Try it yourself
with
Manus
Copy prompt
Using these product photos [files or links] and this audience description [who they are, what they care about], write a [15-30] second video ad script, generate matching b-roll, and add a voiceover in a [tone] voice. Deliver the finished video plus the script as separate files. Do not publish or upload it anywhere; show me the result first.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ArtificialInteligence/comments/1rwghv5/are_people_seriously_having_ai%20automatically_doing_their_business
